title: Erdős Problem #203: no pure finite prime covering with period dividing lcm(1,...,17) = 12,252,240
description:
A partial result on Erdős Problem #203 (erdosproblems.com/203), with its exact certificate and verifiers. Theorem: no pure finite prime covering for Erdős Problem #203 has period dividing N = lcm(1,...,17) = 12,252,240; in particular none has period equal to any of the 480 divisors of N. Of these 480 periods, 411 had already been excluded by earlier work (see below); the remaining 69, from 67,320 up to N (all multiples of 17), are new as far as we know. They are listed in results/NEW_PERIODS.csv, reproduced by verify/new_periods.py: once their pools are computed, 50 have pool density below 1, 18 already fall to the 5/7 cut with uniform weights, and only N itself needs the non-uniform weights of the article.

The complete prime pool, the prime divisors of gcd(2^N-1, 3^N-1) (2,432 bits, 732 decimal digits), consists of 192 primes, the largest 8,168,161. The method (the weighted condition on lines, the slope-one 5/7 cut and the averaging modulo 60) is due to earlier work by Erdős Problem a Day (Patrick White and Claude, 14 October 2026), which also excluded every period up to 65,520 and every divisor of lcm(1,...,16) = 720,720; it builds on the subgroup formula and density condition of AnimishSharma and the complete pools of veljjanoski (erdosproblems.com discussion thread). The new part is the complete N-pool together with explicit non-uniform weights on residues modulo 60, which give the exact bound 3961943/4084080 < 1 and so contradict a covering (uniform weights give 1557209/1531530 > 1). A rational dual certificate shows that the weights are optimal within this fixed cut (direction (1,1), modulus 60, 5/7 normalisation) only.

The record contains the research draft (v1.1, 8 November 2026, revised from v1.0 of 1 November 2026; both versions included; not peer reviewed) with its LaTeX source, the factorisation and per-prime data, the weights and dual certificate as exact rationals, three verifiers and their outputs: a standard-library Python checker (primality, orders, exact bound, dual, divisors), a GMP checker that recomputes the gcd directly, and a from-scratch script that rebuilds the pool, the bound, Lemma 1 for small primes and the dual from N alone; a fourth script determines which divisors of N are new. A verification record lists every documented check.

Scope: this is not a solution of Erdős Problem #203, which remains open. It concerns only pure prime-divisibility coverings and makes no claim about other mechanisms or about the existence of a suitable m.

Use of AI: the research was conceived and directed by the author. As the article states, the author used an AI-assisted workflow, including the author's private research system SAPIO MORPHEUS / COMPLEX and ChatGPT (OpenAI), for algorithm design, computation, checking and preparation of the draft; the PDF carries OpenAI Content Credentials, and the 2026-11-02 checkers were written by ChatGPT/Codex. This record was prepared and the result re-verified with Claude (Anthropic) under the author's direction, including three from-scratch checks by separate Claude agent instances (independent implementations, not an independent human verification). No part of the COMPLEX system is needed to check the result, and none is included. The author is responsible for the content.
